cards.fullLine: Same-origin means the same scheme, host and port.

teaching.text: Two pages on different numbers here never share storage or permissions.

prompt.text: Text from a user turned into HTML can cause cross-site

answer.text: Text from a user turned into HTML can cause cross-site scripting.

hints: It is usually shortened to three letters.
cards.fullLine: Text from a user turned into HTML can cause cross-site scripting.

answer.text: HTTPS protects data in transit between browser and server.

hints: It covers the journey, not the storage at either end.
cards.fullLine: HTTPS protects data in transit between browser and server.

teaching.text: It encrypts the hop but says nothing about the server's trust.

prompt.text: Which response header limits where scripts may load from?

hints: The name names two ideas: content and policy.
cards.fullLine: Content-Security-Policy limits where scripts may load from.

teaching.text: It names the allowed sources for scripts, styles and images.

prompt.text: Which cookie flag hides the cookie from JavaScript?

hints: Only the network layer may read it.
cards.fullLine: The HttpOnly flag hides the cookie from JavaScript.

teaching.text: Even a successful injection cannot read this flag's cookie.

answer.text: A cookie marked Secure is only sent over HTTPS.

cards.fullLine: A cookie marked Secure is only sent over HTTPS.

prompt.text: A form that changes data on another site while you are logged in is what?

hints: The request is genuine; the intent is not.
cards.fullLine: A form that changes data on another site while you are logged in is cross-site request forgery.

teaching.text: The browser attaches the session automatically, so the site must check intent.

prompt.text: User text must reach the page as

cards.fullLine: textContent is the safer way to show a learner's name.
